pilot_process.green_protein_precipitation: green juice heated to regulated 55 C; 15-30 min holding time; centrifuge at approximately 4000 RCF
pilot_process.white_protein_precipitation: 40% w/v food-grade citric-acid solution added by automatic pH control to pH 4; 15-60 min holding time
pilot_process.white_protein_separation: self-unloading disk centrifuge at approximately 8000 RCF

variables.soluble_peak_ABD: mg protein/g dry matter; SE-HPLC RuBisCO-rich peak regions A, B and D
variables.soluble_peak_CE: mg protein/g dry matter; SE-HPLC other peak regions C and E
variables.insoluble_peak_ABD: mg protein/g dry matter; SE-HPLC RuBisCO-rich peak regions A, B and D
variables.insoluble_peak_CE: mg protein/g dry matter; SE-HPLC other peak regions C and E
variables.total_protein: mg protein/g dry matter; source-calculated sum of soluble and insoluble peak areas

uncertainty: Table 3 reports mean and standard deviation for each fraction across the biomass sources; significance letters are the source's Duncan post-hoc groups at p < 0.05.
data_handling: Seven fraction-level rows were transcribed from Table 3. Means, standard deviations, and statistical groups are retained as reported; no values are converted or imputed.
limitations: The eight source materials are cultivated leafy biomass from Sweden, not Dutch roadside grass or GreenHub feed.
The reported results are analytical concentrations per dry mass, not stream flow, total component mass, or recovery efficiency.
High between-material variability and pilot process-specific conditions limit transferability.
The process pH endpoint and citric-acid solution strength are reported, but acid consumption per volume or mass of juice is not; do not infer reagent demand from pH alone.
This source does not establish product market grade, food/feed certification, or GreenHub protein-price eligibility.
suggested_use: Phase 4 reference for fraction-specific soluble/insoluble protein analytical concentrations and product-quality discussion. Not a runtime recovery factor, protein mass balance, reagent-demand parameter, or market-grade specification.
